threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, sectors, and case types for the standardisation project.

messages.text:
Kicking off the Cross-Sector Digital Intake and Case-Handling Standardisation work.

Goal for this thread: agree which case types per sector we include in the first wave and confirm the 30-day timeline and milestones.

From the project brief, we need current-state process maps across health, education, courts and civil service. That aligns with tasks T1–T4 and the shared doc A1.

Initial proposal for scope:
- Medical: outpatient referrals and follow-up appointments
- Education: special support needs applications
- Courts: standard civil claims (no criminal)
- Civil service: general citizen enquiries and complaints

Timeline sketch (within 30 days):
- Days 1–7: document current workflows (T1–T4) and consolidate into A1
- Days 8–15: unified data model and draft forms
- Days 16–23: workflow, SOP and checklists
- Days 24–30: pilot prep and start of pilot

Can each of you confirm if these case types make sense for your area, or suggest a better focus? Once we agree, we can lock D1 and D2.

Thanks for starting this.

For medical, outpatient referrals and follow-up appointments are good candidates. They are frequent and we already have a lot of variation in how intake is done, which shows up in the notes I am preparing for T1.

One nuance: should we include both external referrals from general practitioners and internal referrals between departments, or only external for the first wave? External referrals are more complex but also where we see more errors.

On the timeline, days 1–7 for T1 is feasible from my side, as long as we keep the mapping at a practical level (key steps, actors, forms) as in A1, not every exception.

On the court side, standard civil claims are a sensible starting point.

To keep T3 manageable and aligned with A1, I suggest we narrow further to uncontested monetary claims below a certain value. Those have clear intake rules, standard mandatory documents and well-defined time limits under the civil process order.

If we agree, I will map:
- Intake and registration steps for these claims only
- Mandatory documents (claim form, evidence list, proof of payment, etc.)
- Legal time limits and notification requirements

This should fit in the first 7 days without risking gaps.

Agree that uncontested monetary claims are easier to standardise first.

One question: do we also want to include small claims handled by simplified procedures, or is that a second wave? If we mix them now, T3 might become harder to validate with another officer in time.

I can support with checking the list of mandatory documents once you have a first draft, to make sure it matches our current practice.

For civil service, general citizen enquiries and complaints are fine, but that is still broad.

For T4, I propose we focus on:
- Enquiries submitted via email and web forms
- Written complaints that require a formal response

Walk-in and phone enquiries could be a later wave, since routing rules and transparency requirements are more variable there.

On the 30-day timeline, the phases you outlined look reasonable. We just need to be clear when we expect sign-offs from sector reps so we do not compress the pilot prep at the end.

On medical scope: starting with external referrals only sounds safer for the first wave. Internal referrals can be a follow-up once we see how the unified workflow behaves.

So proposal for medical in D1:
- Include external outpatient referrals and related follow-up appointments
- Exclude internal referrals for now

If that works for you, we can lock that in and reflect it in T1 and later in the unified workflow.

External referrals plus their follow-up appointments works for me.

I will document T1 with that scope: end-to-end from receipt of the external referral to scheduling and initial follow-up, including the current forms and common errors.

Please note that some consent forms differ by specialty; I will flag those in the process map so we can see later how they fit into the unified intake approach.

Good point on simplified small claims.

For the first wave, I suggest we limit D1 on the court side to uncontested monetary claims under the standard procedure only. Simplified small claims can be a second wave once we have tested the unified intake with the more straightforward category.

I will reflect that in T3 and make sure the process map in A1 clearly states the scope.

Limiting to uncontested monetary claims under the standard procedure is fine by me.

I will be available to do the second validation step for T3 once you have the first version ready, so we can keep the schedule.

I am aligned with focusing T4 on email and web enquiries plus written complaints.

For D1 on civil service, we can phrase it as:
- Include email and web enquiries that create a case record
- Include written complaints requiring a formal written response
- Exclude phone-only and walk-in enquiries for the first wave

I will map routing, escalation and transparency requirements for those channels in T4.

On education, I proposed special support needs applications, but I realise we also have school enrolment and scholarship applications.

Given the 30-day window, I suggest we keep D1 for education to special support needs applications only. They have clearer policy constraints and approval steps, which fits T2 and will be easier to map in A1.

If no objections, I will proceed with T2 on that basis.

Focusing education on special support needs applications makes sense from a cross-sector view. Those cases often interact with medical and sometimes court processes, so having a clear intake there will help later alignment.

From my side, no objection to that scope for D1.
No objection from courts either. Narrowing each sector to one or two well-defined case types should make the unified workflow more realistic to implement within 30 days.

Summarising D1 based on the discussion so far:
- Medical: external outpatient referrals and related follow-up appointments
- Education: special support needs applications
- Courts: uncontested monetary civil claims under the standard procedure
- Civil service: email and web enquiries that create a case record, plus written complaints requiring a formal written response

Unless anyone sees a gap, I will treat this as the agreed scope for the first standardisation wave and reflect it in T1–T4 and A1.

Works for me.

On D2, can we be more explicit about milestones and who needs to review what? That will help me plan availability on the civil service side.

Good point. Here is a more concrete D2 proposal within the 30 days:

- By end of day 7: T1–T4 completed and consolidated into A1
- By end of day 12: draft unified data model (T5) shared as A2
- By end of day 18: sector form drafts ready (T6, T7) and reviewed
- By end of day 23: unified workflow and SOP drafted (T9) and checklists drafted (T10)
- By end of day 30: pilot plan prepared (T11), initial pilot started, and feedback log A6 set up for T12

Reviews:
- Medical and court reps review A2 and sector forms
- All sectors review the SOP and checklists

If this looks realistic, we can confirm D2.

From the medical side, the milestones look achievable.

I can complete T1 by day 5 to give a bit of buffer, and I can also start sketching T6 once A2 is in a stable draft, so we are not rushing near day 18.

No concerns on D2 from me.

The timeline works for courts as well.

I will aim to finalise T3 by day 6, including validation by another officer, so that A1 is ready for use in T5 without delay.

No objections to D2.

From civil service, the dates are fine. I will plan T4 to be done by day 7 and will block time around days 23–24 to review the SOP and checklists.

Happy to confirm D2 as proposed.

Thanks all.

To close this thread:
- D1: scope for the first standardisation wave is confirmed for all four sectors as summarised in M14
- D2: 30-day timeline and milestones are confirmed as in M16, with minor accelerations where possible

I will update the shared overview for the Cross-Sector Digital Intake and Case-Handling Standardisation project and reflect these in the descriptions of T1–T4 and the plan for A1.

threads.thread_goal: Review and finalise the unified intake data model and standard forms.

messages.text:
I have uploaded a first draft of the unified intake data model and field inventory as A2, based on the current-state maps in A1 and the scope we agreed in D1.

This covers T5 and is structured as:
- Common person and case identifiers
- Sector-neutral intake details
- Sector-specific sections for medical, education, courts and civil service

I would like feedback from each of you on:
1) Any missing mandatory fields for your sector
2) Fields that are unnecessary or too detailed for frontline staff
3) Anything that might conflict with your legal or policy requirements

Once we converge on A2, we can move to T6 and T7 for the sector forms.

Please add comments directly in A2 and use this thread to flag any bigger concerns before we move to D3 and D4.

I have gone through the medical section of A2.

Positives:
- The common identifiers and contact details look fine
- The referral reason and urgency fields align with what we use today

Gaps and suggestions:
- We need a clear field for referring practitioner identifier (not just free text name) for traceability and insurance checks
- Consent: there should be a structured field indicating whether the patient has signed the current consent form, plus date
- For T6, we should avoid free text for diagnosis at intake; a short list of categories plus an optional notes field will reduce variation

None of this conflicts with our current healthcare administration rules, but I would like to double-check with our data protection contact before we finalise D3.

I reviewed the court section in A2 with the civil process order in mind.

Observations:
- Mandatory party details and case type fields are present
- We need explicit fields for: value of the claim, interest calculation basis, and whether legal representation is involved
- Evidence: instead of a single free text field, we should have a structured list (document type, date, reference number) to support T7

Also, legal time limits and notification requirements are not fields themselves but depend on case type and filing date. I suggest we store filing date and case type in A2 and handle the calculation in the workflow and checklists later.

No legal conflicts spotted so far, but I will do a second pass before we sign off D3.

Agree with the need for structured evidence fields.

One more detail: we should include a field indicating whether any protective measures or confidentiality restrictions apply to the file. Even if the detailed rules sit in the guideline later, the intake form needs a simple yes or no plus a short description.

I have added a comment in A2 to that effect.

From the civil service side, A2 looks mostly fine.

I have two concerns:
- Some of the optional demographic fields might be sensitive and not strictly needed for handling email enquiries and written complaints
- We should have a simple field for whether the enquiry is a request for information, a complaint, or a suggestion, to support routing and transparency reporting

I have marked these in A2. As long as we keep the form simple for frontline staff, I am comfortable moving towards D3 once we adjust these points.

Thanks for the detailed comments.

I will update A2 to:
- Add a structured field for referring practitioner identifier
- Add a consent status field with date
- Replace free text diagnosis at intake with a short list plus notes

Once that is in place, we can reflect these in the medical form under T6.

On the data protection check, I suggest we capture any concerns in the confidentiality guideline thread as well, so we stay consistent.

For the court section, I will:
- Add fields for claim value, interest basis, and representation
- Change the evidence field to a repeatable structure (type, date, reference)
- Keep filing date and case type as the basis for time limit calculations in the workflow rather than as separate fields

I will also add the protective measures indicator suggested in M24.

Once I push these changes to A2, could you both do a quick re-check so we can move towards D3?

On civil service fields, I will:
- Remove or mark as optional the more sensitive demographic fields that are not needed for handling the enquiry
- Add a simple enquiry type field (information request, complaint, suggestion) as you propose

This should keep the intake form manageable for staff while still supporting reporting.

I will post here once the updated A2 is ready for a final pass.

I have rechecked the medical section in the updated A2.

The new fields for practitioner identifier and consent look good, and the diagnosis categories are clear enough for intake staff.

From my side, the data model now supports what we need for T6 without adding unnecessary complexity. I am comfortable moving towards D3, assuming the data protection officer does not raise any new issues.

I have reviewed the updated court section in A2.

The added fields for claim value, interest basis, representation and structured evidence cover our legal requirements for the scope we defined.

I see no conflicts with the civil process order for these case types. From my side, A2 is ready for D3, and we can start drafting the court intake form under T7 based on this structure.

I confirm that the protective measures indicator and the structured evidence fields in A2 look correct.

This will make it easier later to ensure that any confidentiality restrictions are visible at intake and can be linked to the guideline.

I have checked the civil service section in the updated A2.

The enquiry type field is clear, and the sensitive demographic fields are now optional or removed, which should help with adoption.

From my side, A2 is acceptable for D3.

Thanks for all the reviews.

To close D3: we agree to approve the unified intake data model and minimum data set in A2 for the case types defined in D1, with the sector-specific adjustments discussed above.

Next, we need to sign off the sector-specific digital intake forms for pilot use under D4. I propose the following approach:
- Medical form (T6) and court form (T7) to be drafted directly from A2
- Education and civil service forms to reuse the common sections and add only the minimal sector-specific fields

I will share initial form drafts shortly for your review.

I have created a first draft of the medical intake form for T6, using the fields from A2.

Key points:
- Form is in the agreed office format
- Sections follow the patient journey: identification, referral details, consent, scheduling
- Confidentiality and consent text is aligned with our current templates

I have tested it with two sample cases and noted a couple of layout tweaks, but functionally it works.

Please confirm if this is sufficient for D4 on the medical side, or if you want any additional checks before we mark it ready for pilot.

I have drafted the court intake form for T7 based on A2.

Structure:
- Party and representative details
- Case type and claim value
- Filing date and interest basis
- Structured evidence list
- Indicator for protective measures or confidentiality restrictions

I have checked it against our current court procedures and the civil process order for the selected case types. Another court officer will review it today to complete the approval step in T7.

Assuming no major issues, I consider the court form ready for D4.

I have reviewed the court intake form draft.

Everything aligns with the fields in A2 and our current practice. I have only suggested minor wording changes in the evidence section.

From my side, the form is ready for pilot and can be included in D4.

I have adapted the civil service form using A2.

It keeps the common identification and contact fields, plus:
- Enquiry type (information request, complaint, suggestion)
- Channel (email or web)
- Simple routing and escalation indicators

The layout is one page and should be manageable for staff.

I am comfortable including this in D4 for the pilot.

I have now also drafted the education intake form for special support needs applications, aligned with A2.

It includes:
- Student and guardian details
- Education setting and grade
- Summary of support needs and existing assessments
- Policy-related approval steps as checkboxes

Given the confirmations above, I propose we close D4 as follows:
- Approve the medical, education, court and civil service digital intake forms, all based on A2, for use in the upcoming pilot.

Unless there are objections today, I will record D4 as approved and move the related tasks T6 and T7 to ready for pilot.

No objections from medical.

The current T6 form draft is ready for pilot from my side.

Confirmed from courts as well.

T7 is ready for pilot, and I support closing D4 as you propose.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on confidentiality rules and how they apply in the new workflow.

messages.text:
I have posted a draft of the cross-sector confidentiality and data handling guideline as A3, based on T8.

The structure is:
- Shared principles across health, education, courts and civil service
- Sector-specific rules and legal references
- Access control and document sharing practices
- Practical examples for the case types in D1

Please review with a focus on:
- Any conflicts with your sector rules
- Gaps where staff might be unsure what they can share and with whom
- How this should link to the intake forms and workflow

Once we are aligned, we can move to D5 and formally approve the guideline.

I have reviewed A3 from the medical perspective.

Strengths:
- The shared principles on minimum necessary data and purpose limitation are clear
- The section on sharing with education and civil service for support cases is helpful

Concerns:
- For external referrals, we need explicit wording that medical diagnoses and detailed clinical notes are not to be shared beyond health unless there is a clear legal basis and documented consent
- The examples should show how to handle situations where a patient withdraws consent after intake

I have added comments in A3. Once we adjust those, I am comfortable aligning this with the medical intake form and workflow.

From the court side, A3 is broadly consistent with our obligations.

Points to refine:
- We should clarify that court case files are generally public to the extent allowed by law, but that certain documents (e.g. medical reports, minors data) may have restricted access
- The guideline should reference how protective measures flagged at intake (as per A2 and T7) translate into access restrictions in practice

I have suggested wording in A3. With those changes, I see no conflict with our legal framework.

I support the additions proposed.

One more suggestion: include a short checklist in A3 for court staff on when to mark a file as restricted, linked to the protective measures field in the intake form.

This will help ensure consistent application of the rules.

Looking at A3 from the education side:

- The general principles are fine
- For special support needs, we should be explicit that only the minimum necessary health information is shared with schools, and that detailed medical reports stay within health unless there is explicit consent or a legal requirement
- It might help to add an example where a school requests more information than is strictly needed, and how staff should respond

I have added these as comments in A3.

Thanks for the detailed feedback.

I will update A3 to:
- Add explicit wording on not sharing detailed diagnoses or clinical notes beyond health without a clear legal basis and documented consent
- Include an example on handling withdrawal of consent after intake

I will also cross-reference the consent fields in A2 and the medical form so staff know where to record this.

For the court-related points, I will:
- Clarify in A3 the general public nature of court files and the exceptions
- Add a section explaining how the protective measures indicator from A2 and T7 leads to restricted access in the case management system
- Include a short checklist, as suggested in M44, on when to mark a file as restricted

This should make the link between intake and confidentiality rules more concrete.

On the education side, I will:
- Add explicit language on minimum necessary health information shared with schools
- Include an example where a school requests more information than needed and how staff should respond, including when to escalate

I will ping the data protection officer informally to see if they spot any issues with the updated wording before we move to D5.

I have rechecked the updated medical-related sections in A3.

The new wording on sharing diagnoses and handling consent withdrawal is clear and matches our current practice.

From my side, the guideline is now usable for training and for linking to the medical intake workflow.

I have reviewed the court-related updates in A3.

The explanation of public access versus restricted documents and the checklist for marking files as restricted are accurate.

This aligns with how we handle sensitive evidence today, so I see no remaining issues from the court side.

The checklist in A3 is very helpful.

I think this will reduce uncertainty for newer staff when they process cases with protective measures.

I have checked the education-related updates in A3.

The examples and the emphasis on minimum necessary information are clear. I will make sure the education intake form and later the SOP reference this guideline explicitly.

Given the latest updates and your confirmations, I propose we close D5 as follows:

- Approve A3 as the cross-sector confidentiality and data handling guideline for the case types in D1
- Use A3 as the single reference for confidentiality rules in the unified workflow, forms and training materials

Unless there are objections by tomorrow, I will mark D5 as approved and version A3 accordingly.

threads.thread_goal: Validate the unified intake workflow, SOP, and frontline checklists.

messages.text:
I have shared a draft of the unified intake workflow and SOP as A4, covering the case types in D1, and initial one-page frontline checklists as A5.

This corresponds to T9 and T10.

The workflow in A4 is structured in phases:
- Receive and register intake
- Verify completeness and eligibility
- Apply confidentiality checks using A3
- Route and schedule
- Confirm to the citizen or referring party

The checklists in A5 are sector-specific but follow the same structure.

Please test the SOP and checklists with one or two sample cases in your area and share:
- Steps that are unclear or missing
- Any conflicts with your current mandatory procedures
- Suggestions to simplify the checklists for frontline staff

We need to converge here before we can approve D6 and D7.

I have tested A4 and the medical checklist in A5 with two sample external referrals.

Findings:
- The receive and register steps match our practice
- The completeness check is helpful, but we should explicitly mention verifying insurance details and consent status before scheduling
- The confidentiality step should reference the specific consent field in the medical form and A3

I have suggested wording changes in A4 and A5. Once those are in, the SOP will be workable for medical staff.

I ran through A4 and the court checklist in A5 with a sample uncontested monetary claim.

Observations:
- The general flow fits, but we need to emphasise the legal time limit check earlier in the process, right after registration
- The checklist should include a step to verify that all mandatory documents listed in T7 are present before accepting the filing
- The confidentiality step should remind staff to check the protective measures indicator

I have added comments in A4 and A5 accordingly.

I agree with moving the legal time limit check earlier.

Also, in the court checklist in A5, we might want to add a short reminder about how to handle incomplete filings: either request missing documents or reject, depending on the rules.

I have suggested a brief note in the checklist.

I tested A4 and the civil service checklist in A5 with a sample email enquiry and a written complaint.

Feedback:
- The routing step is clear, but we should add a reminder to log the enquiry type (information request, complaint, suggestion) as per A2
- For complaints, the checklist should include a step to check statutory response deadlines and any transparency requirements

I have added these points as comments in A4 and A5.

Thanks for the tests.

I will update A4 and the medical checklist in A5 to:
- Add explicit insurance and consent verification in the completeness step
- Reference the consent field in the medical form and A3 in the confidentiality step

Once updated, could you do a quick re-run with one of your sample cases to confirm the flow feels natural for staff?

For the court flow, I will:
- Move the legal time limit check to immediately after registration in A4
- Add a checklist item in A5 to verify all mandatory documents from T7 before accepting the filing
- Include a reminder to check the protective measures indicator and apply the A3 rules

I will also incorporate the note on handling incomplete filings from M57.

On the civil service side, I will:
- Add a step in A4 and A5 to log the enquiry type as per A2
- Include a reminder to check response deadlines and transparency requirements for complaints

This should make the checklist more actionable without adding too much detail.

I have re-tested the updated medical flow in A4 and the checklist in A5 with one of the sample referrals.

The added insurance and consent checks fit naturally into the process, and the reference to A3 is clear.

From my side, the SOP and checklist are ready for pilot use in the medical area.

I have rechecked the court flow and checklist.

The earlier time limit check and the explicit document verification step work well. The note on incomplete filings is also accurate.

I consider the court parts of A4 and A5 ready for the pilot.

I confirm that the updated court checklist in A5 is clear and practical.

This should help frontline staff avoid missing key steps when registering claims.

I have re-tested the civil service flow with the updated A4 and A5.

Logging the enquiry type and checking response deadlines are now clearly integrated.

From my side, the SOP and checklist are ready for use in the pilot.

Given the feedback and re-tests, I propose we close:
- D6: approve A4 as the unified intake workflow and SOP for pilot implementation across the agreed case types
- D7: approve the frontline checklists in A5 for each sector as the reference tools for staff during the pilot

If there are no objections by end of day, I will mark D6 and D7 as approved and update T9 and T10 status accordingly.

threads.thread_goal: Plan the pilot, track issues, and agree on improvement actions.

messages.text:
With the forms, guideline and SOP in place, we need to finalise the pilot plan.

I have started the pilot planning and tracking sheet as A6, linked to T11 and T12.

Proposal for pilot scope and schedule:
- Duration: 2 weeks within our 30-day window
- Medical: 10 external referrals and related follow-ups
- Education: 10 special support needs applications
- Courts: 10 uncontested monetary claims
- Civil service: 20 email or web enquiries and 10 written complaints

Tracking in A6:
- Basic case details (no sensitive content)
- Whether the new forms and checklists were used
- Issues encountered and quick fixes applied

We also need to agree on criteria for success and how we will consolidate feedback for the final report A7.

Please share any concerns with this scope or suggestions for success criteria so we can close D8.

From the medical side, 10 external referrals plus follow-ups over 2 weeks is realistic.

For success criteria, I suggest we track:
- Percentage of referrals with complete mandatory fields at first submission
- Number of corrections needed compared to our baseline
- Staff feedback on ease of use of the form and checklist

I have added these as columns and notes in A6.

For courts, 10 uncontested monetary claims is fine.

Additional success criteria to consider:
- Number of filings rejected or delayed due to missing documents
- Time from filing to completion of intake registration

These can be captured in A6 without storing sensitive content.

I have added draft fields for these metrics.

I support those metrics.

We might also want a simple flag in A6 for cases where confidentiality rules from A3 were particularly relevant, so we can see if the guideline and checklists are clear enough in practice.

For education, 10 special support needs applications over 2 weeks is manageable.

I suggest we track:
- Whether all required approvals are captured in the form and SOP steps
- Any confusion about what information can be shared with schools, referencing A3

I have added these as notes in A6 so we can include them in the consolidation under T12 and the final report A7.

Thanks for the suggestions.

I have incorporated the medical and court metrics into A6, including the confidentiality relevance flag from M70.

For civil service, I propose we also track:
- Whether the enquiry type and channel were correctly recorded
- Whether response deadlines were met for complaints

I will add these fields as well.

The additional civil service metrics make sense.

From my side, the pilot scope and tracking approach in A6 look complete enough to move forward.

Agreed.

The current A6 structure should give us enough information to identify issues and improvements without overburdening staff.
I have added a short note in A6 on how to mark cases where confidentiality rules were a key factor, so we remember to look at those specifically when consolidating feedback in T12.

I will take the lead on T12 later, so I have added a section in A6 to tag issues by category: process, template, training.

This should make it easier to build A7 at the end of the pilot.

To close D8, here is a summary of what we have agreed:

Pilot scope:
- 2-week pilot
- Medical: 10 external referrals and follow-ups
- Education: 10 special support needs applications
- Courts: 10 uncontested monetary claims
- Civil service: 20 email or web enquiries and 10 written complaints

Tracking approach:
- Use A6 to log basic case details, usage of forms and checklists, issues and quick fixes
- Capture metrics on completeness, rework, time to register, confidentiality relevance, and sector-specific points

Criteria for success:
- Majority of cases processed using the new forms and SOP without major incidents
- Reduction in missing mandatory information compared to baseline
- Staff feedback indicating that forms and checklists are usable

Unless there are objections, I will record D8 as confirmed and finalise T11 accordingly.

No objections from medical.

I will brief the relevant staff on the pilot scope and how to log cases in A6.

Confirmed from courts as well.

I will inform the team about the pilot cases and ensure they record the required data in A6.

All good from education.

Once the pilot is underway, I will start preparing the structure for consolidating feedback under T12 so we can move quickly towards A7 at the end.
